response:
Diagnosis driving this batch. The archive now discriminates sharply between construction families. Level-of-investment sorts (gen-0 multiplicative gates) give strong FMB slopes and zero or perverse FF5 alpha. Cross-sectional mix ratios (AcquiredShare, BoughtVersusBuilt, ShiftTowardBuying) give neither once coverage is repaired — the point mass at zero for non-acquirers dominates. What actually works is **within-firm timing contrasts**: CapacityPushAgainstMarginErosion (own-history rank of capex intensity minus own-history rank of gross margin) is the best joint result so far (fmb −4.92, alpha −2.6%/yr, t −2.99, Sharpe −0.27), and PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending, the other own-history construction, is the best positive-signed result (alpha +4.1%, fmb +1.88). The one large alpha from a level construction (AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears, −5.5%, t −4.8) has a near-binary R&D leg, i.e. it is partly an R&D-reporting dummy, which is exactly why its FMB slope is flat. So this generation (i) builds a timing-contrast matrix that identifies *which* investment channel the effect lives in while holding construction fixed, (ii) repairs the persistence signal by replacing binary counts with continuous cumulative intensities, and (iii) removes R&D-reporting-status contamination by using uncoalesced xrd where the hypothesis is about innovators, and adds one new second-moment mechanism.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, MA(sale, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Among firms that run research programs, those currently at a five-year high in research intensity while physical investment sits at a five-year low are reallocating toward knowledge capital, and because the research leg is expensed while the retrenched capex leg reads as contraction, the market underreacts.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This applies the winning own-history-rank construction to the two investment channels directly, so both legs are [0,1] within-firm percentiles and neither dollar magnitude nor industry membership can dominate — the flaw that broke the earlier difference-in-changes substitution index. Using xrd uncoalesced deliberately restricts the sample to innovators, which removes the R&D-reporting-status contamination the critic identified in the peak-relative and count-based signals, so the sort is a genuine intra-firm reallocation test.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: CumulativeAcquisitionMinusResearchIntensity
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 5), TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Over a five-year window, firms that have devoted more of their asset base to buying companies than to building knowledge internally have accumulated capability at market prices rather than at cost, and this cumulative sourcing tilt predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This isolates one design choice relative to the archived AcquirerYearsMinusInnovatorYears, which produced the largest FF5 alpha (−5.5%, t −4.8) but a flat FMB slope: replacing the two near-binary year-counts with continuous, commonly scaled cumulative intensities should restore cross-sectional slope information while keeping the same cumulative-strategy mechanism. If the alpha survives the change, the effect is genuine sourcing intensity; if it collapses, the archived alpha was an R&D-reporting dummy, which is itself a decisive diagnosis.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: InventoryBuildAgainstMarginErosion
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, MA(sale, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Physical stock-building is only warranted when the firm's product differentiation is intact; a firm whose inventory relative to sales is at a five-year high precisely when its gross margin is at a five-year low is pushing goods into a market that is no longer paying for them, and future markdowns follow.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This moves the winning timing-contrast construction to the working-capital channel, which was the other flow signal with a real FMB slope (InventoryBuildPerGrossProfit, fmb −3.0), while eliminating the objection that a level ratio of capex to gross profit is a mechanical quotient of two published anomalies — both legs here are own-history ranks, so cross-sectional inventory intensity and cross-sectional gross profitability are differenced out. Testing plant and inventory under identical construction tells us whether the mechanism is capacity-specific or a general physical-overexpansion-into-commoditization effect.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: GoodwillAccumulationAgainstMarginErosion
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(gdwl, ADD(ppent, gdwl)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Purchased intangible capital only retains its carrying value if the acquired businesses keep earning rents; firms whose capital base has drifted to a five-year maximum in goodwill share exactly while gross margin has drifted to a five-year minimum carry unrecognized impairment exposure that is priced with a lag.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The archived goodwill-impairment attempt failed on the FMB side because it multiplied a goodwill share by a noisy one-year revenue-growth gate; recasting both legs as own-history ranks removes the outlier-driven gate and the age/size drift the critic flagged in the cumulative goodwill ratio. Leaving gdwl uncoalesced restricts the test to firms that actually have purchased capital at risk, so the short leg is the pre-writedown cohort rather than a mass of non-acquirers.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: InvestmentMixInstability
EXPRESSION: VOL(RATIO(xrd, ADD(capx, xrd)), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that keeps swinging the split of its investment budget between plant and research lacks a stable strategy or is financially constrained into stop-start project funding, and such instability in intangible commitment destroys the option value of research and predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This is a second-moment mechanism entirely absent from the archive: the signal is zero-information about the *level* of either investment channel and only measures the stability of their mix, so it is orthogonal to CMA, to R&D intensity, and to the timing contrasts elsewhere in this batch. Restricting to firms reporting both capex and R&D keeps the ratio well defined and avoids the degenerate zero-volatility mass that coalescing would create for non-innovators.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: ResearchPushAgainstMarginErosion
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, MA(sale, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: When margins are compressing, the firm's response matters: raising research intensity is adaptation that builds new intangible advantage and is rewarded, whereas raising physical capacity in the same situation is doubling down on a commoditizing business and is punished.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is the deliberate mirror image of the archive's best signal — identical construction, identical margin-timing leg, with the investment channel switched from plant to research — so the pair provides the cleanest possible test of the central premise of this theme pairing, that tangible and intangible investment carry opposite return implications under the same conditions. A positive alpha here alongside the negative alpha of the capex version would establish the interaction as a genuine investment-type effect rather than a general investment-timing effect.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---CRITIQUE KnowledgeVersusPlantInvestmentTiming---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: A defensible reconstruction of the archived PeakRelativeKnowledgeVersusPlantSpending (which was borderline at t 1.78) using the better-behaved own-history-rank machinery rather than peak ratios, though it remains the same reallocation hypothesis and the xrd/MA(sale,3) leg mechanically rises when sales fall, so part of any long-leg return may be a sales-decline/value confound rather than genuine intangible reallocation.

---CRITIQUE CumulativeAcquisitionMinusResearchIntensity---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The two legs are differenced in raw, unranked at-scaled units with very unequal dispersion (five-year cumulative xrd/at is far larger and more persistent than aqc/at for the R&D-reporting subsample), so the composite will be dominated by minus R&D intensity — i.e. essentially a restatement of the published R&D-intensity/R&D-to-market anomaly — rather than testing the sourcing-mix mechanism it claims.

---CRITIQUE InventoryBuildAgainstMarginErosion---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: A coherent, internally consistent transfer of the archive's best-performing timing-contrast construction to the working-capital channel where an independent FMB slope already existed, with both legs demeaned within firm so it is not simply a repackaging of the known inventory-growth or gross-profitability anomalies, and the sign follows naturally from the expression.

---CRITIQUE GoodwillAccumulationAgainstMarginErosion---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: gdwl/(ppent+gdwl) drifts upward almost mechanically because goodwill is not depreciated while net plant is, so its five-year TS_RANK will be pinned near its maximum with heavy ties for most acquirers, collapsing the signal into roughly the negative of a margin-timing rank and thus testing profitability deterioration rather than impairment exposure.

---CRITIQUE InvestmentMixInstability---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Genuinely a new second-moment mechanism for this pairing and internally consistent, but the volatility of a bounded ratio with lumpy small denominators will load heavily on firm size and general cash-flow/earnings volatility — already-documented return predictors — so the result will need a size and fundamental-volatility control to be interpretable.

---CRITIQUE ResearchPushAgainstMarginErosion---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The symmetry argument is the right kind of discriminating test, but the construction is not actually the mirror of the winning signal: scaling R&D by MA(sale,3) while the margin leg is also a sales-based ratio means a sales contraction pushes leg one up and leg two down simultaneously, so the signal mechanically maxes out for deteriorating-revenue firms and any positive slope is confounded with value/distress rather than identifying intangible adaptation (scaling xrd by MA(at,3) would fix this).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: AcquisitionSourcingRankVersusResearchSourcingRank
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at), 5), NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 5)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that have sourced their capability over the past five years mainly by purchasing companies rather than by funding internal research have paid market prices for intangibles, and this cumulative sourcing tilt predicts lower returns than an equally sized internally funded program.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: The flagged version differenced two at-scaled cumulative intensities with very unequal dispersion, so it degenerated into minus R&D intensity; rank-standardizing each leg before differencing forces the two channels to contribute equally, which is the minimal change that actually identifies the sourcing mix. The two legs are not independent bets but two mutually exclusive ways of buying the same thing — capability — so their rank difference is a composition measure, and it isolates the continuous-intensity design choice against the archived binary year-count version that produced a −5.5% alpha with a flat FMB slope.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: GoodwillOverhangWithRealInvestmentRetreat
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(gdwl, MA(SUB(sale, cogs), 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, MA(ppent, 3)), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: Acquired intangible capital is impaired in economic terms when it stops generating rents; firms whose goodwill is at a five-year high relative to the gross profit it produces, while their physical reinvestment rate is at a five-year low, are harvesting rather than sustaining acquired businesses and face writedowns and disappointment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Scaling goodwill by gross profit rather than by net plant removes the mechanical upward drift the critic identified — goodwill over plant rises automatically because plant depreciates, whereas goodwill over gross profit rises only when acquisitions fail to deliver rents, so the own-history rank is no longer pinned at its maximum with ties. Replacing the margin leg with the firm's own physical reinvestment rank also means the signal is no longer approximately the negative of a profitability-timing rank, so it tests acquired-capital overhang jointly with real-investment retreat rather than re-testing margin deterioration.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: ResearchPushUnderMarginPressure
EXPRESSION: SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(xrd, MA(at, 3)), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5))
HYPOTHESIS: When gross margins are compressing, firms that respond by pushing research intensity to a five-year high are adapting and rebuilding intangible advantage, and this response is rewarded, in contrast to firms that respond by pushing physical capacity to a five-year high.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Rescaling the research leg by a three-year average asset base, exactly matching the capex-over-plant scaling of the winning capex version, removes the confound the critic identified: a sales contraction no longer mechanically raises leg one while lowering leg two, so the signal cannot max out purely on deteriorating-revenue firms. With that fix the proposal becomes a true mirror of the archive's best signal, holding construction, window and margin leg fixed and switching only the investment channel, which is the sharpest available test of whether tangible and intangible investment carry opposite implications under identical conditions.
